cohort: 440 children (49.3% girls, 24.8% born by cesarean delivery; all children except for 6 were breastfed for varying durations; median 40 weeks; interquartile range, 30-53 weeks)
finding: Fecal microbiota composition was associated with development of atopic dermatitis, allergic sensitization, and asthma, with members of the Lachnospiraceae family, as well as the genera Faecalibacterium and Dialister, being associated with a reduced risk of atopy.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery, compared with cesarean delivery, was most strongly associated with an enrichment of Bacteroides species at 5 weeks through 31 weeks.
